The design emphasizes stable long-term operation with corrosion control, cathodic protection on subsea assets, and redundancy for critical systems.

platforms.field: The K04-A field is a shallow conventional gas reservoir in the Dutch sector producing natural gas from Lower Permian formations. Connected with the broader K4b/K5a block developments, the field’s reserves are developed with multiple small platforms and subsea tie-backs feeding central processing.
platforms.intro: K4A is a satellite gas production platform in the Dutch North Sea, brought onstream in the late 1990s as part of the K4/K5 area development. It collects gas from nearby wells and routes it to central processing facilities such as K5P or similar hubs.
platforms.fac: The K4A installation comprises a steel jacket with well slots tied to subsea completions. It lacks full processing capability, instead routing unprocessed gas through pipelines to a nearby processing platform (e.g., K5P or equivalent). The platform includes basic metering and flow control, with remote monitoring and safety systems. Gas export flows through subsea pipelines integrated into the K4/K5 area network, then into the national export grid. Utilities for K4A focus on control umbilicals, emergency shutdown, and minimal local power for sensors and communication.

platforms.field: The reservoir targeted by K4BE is part of the K4b gas accumulations in shallow North Sea waters. These conventional gas reservoirs are developed with multiple unmanned platforms producing to central facilities.
platforms.intro: K4BE is a small satellite gas platform in the K4/K5 cluster on the Dutch continental shelf, installed around 2000. It collects production from designated wells and routes that gas to central processing platforms.
platforms.fac: K4BE has a steel jacket and topsides configured for well access, flow control, and pipeline export to a primary processing hub. No major separation or compression equipment resides on the platform; it functions as a wellhead and manifold station. Gas is metered and sent through subsea pipelines to larger installations where separation, dehydration, and compression occur. The platform’s utilities are limited to remote control, shutdown systems, and minimal electrical supply for communication and instrumentation.

platforms.field: The K5b cluster overlaps with the K05a-B conventional gas field in shallow North Sea waters. Reservoirs produce natural gas from Permian formations, developed through a network of wellheads and platforms feeding central processing.
platforms.intro: K5-CU is an unmanned gas platform built as part of the K5b cluster on the Dutch North Sea shelf, installed around 2010. It serves as a collection and conduit point for gas wells in the area, linking them into the broader transport network.
platforms.fac: K5-CU includes a steel jacket and topsides with slots for wells and manifold headers. Gas gathered here is routed through export pipelines to nearby processing hubs rather than processed in-situ. Facilities focus on flow control, metering, and safe shutdown systems managed remotely. Electrical systems power instrumentation and communications. Export pipelines connect K5-CU into the existing K-area infrastructure, which in turn ties into higher-capacity trunk pipelines to shore.

platforms.field: The K05a-B conventional gas field comprises reservoirs in shallow North Sea waters producing gas from Permian Slochteren formation. The field development includes multiple small platforms tied into a central processing and export network.
platforms.intro: K5A and K5B are wellhead and satellite gas platforms in the Dutch North Sea K5a/K5b blocks, installed mid-1990s. They gather natural gas from multiple wells and feed central processing infrastructure within the K4/K5 area.
platforms.fac: K5A/B consist of steel jacket structures with well slots and subsea completions. They function as collection hubs that route unprocessed gas to a central processing platform (e.g., K5P or equivalent). There are no large separation trains on K5A/B; instead, basic metering and flow control equipment is installed. Export of collected gas occurs via subsea pipelines integrated into the K-area infrastructure, leading to onshore export lines. Control and utility systems enable remote operations, safety shutdown, and communication with central processing installations.

platforms.field: The part of the K05a-B gas field associated with K5D consists of conventional shallow-water Permian reservoirs. Development uses small platforms and subsea tie-backs to central processing hubs, with export via trunk pipelines.
platforms.intro: K5D is a satellite gas platform within the K5a/K5b block complex in the Dutch North Sea, installed in the mid-1990s. It collects gas from designated wells and feeds it to larger processing installations in the area.
platforms.fac: K5D comprises a steel jacket with well access, basic metering, and flow control. The platform does not host full gas processing; instead, unprocessed gas is transported via subsea pipelines to central facilities where separation, dehydration, and compression occur. K5D’s utilities include remote monitoring, emergency shutdown, and minimal local power for instrumentation. Export gas ties into the K-area pipeline network and onward to onshore export systems.

platforms.field: The K05/K05a gas fields are conventional offshore gas accumulations in the Netherlands sector, located ~115-km northwest of Den Helder. Discovered in the late 20th century and brought onstream from the early 1990s, these fields produce gas from shallow Permian Rotliegend sandstones. Reservoirs have multiple satellite platforms tied back to central facilities.
platforms.intro: A fixed normally unmanned gas wellhead and manifold platform in the K05 area of the Dutch North Sea. Installed in 1997, it serves as a satellite node within the K05/K05a gas field cluster, routing well fluids toward the central processing hub at K5-P and other collection points. It does not house major processing modules.
platforms.fac: K5EN/C hosts wellheads and manifolds for a small number of production wells. Unlike central platforms, it lacks large separation trains, compressors, or dehydration skids; produced gas flows via subsea flowlines and risers to K5-P and adjacent processing installations. The platform’s utility systems are sized for unmanned operation, including power for instrumentation and safety systems, emergency shutdown valves, and remote control/monitoring. Flow control and subsea tie-ins manage well outputs and ensure safe hand-off to central processing. Gas exports from the broader K05 area proceed through integrated subsea pipelines into the Dutch export network.

platforms.field: The K05/K05a offshore gas fields are conventional shallow-water accumulations in the Dutch North Sea. Reservoirs are primarily Rotliegend sandstones with multiple satellite wellheads feeding central production and export infrastructure. The field was developed in the early 1990s and has remained a stable gas producer via clustered platforms and pipeline networks.
platforms.intro: A fixed steel gas production and processing platform in the K05 block, installed in 1993. It is the central production hub in the K05/K05a cluster, supporting gas gathering, separation, and export functions. The platform includes limited accommodation and links to satellite platforms such as K5EN/C and K5PK.
platforms.fac: K5P houses the core processing facilities for the K05 area: wellheads feed into three-phase separation, gas dehydration (to meet pipeline specs), metering, and pressure boosting/compression equipment to prepare gas for export. The platform also supports drilling operations on its own slots and collects flows from satellites including K5EN/C and K5PK via subsea flowlines or bridgelinks. Utility systems include power generation for processing and safety systems, chemical injection for hydrate control and corrosion inhibition, produced water management, and remote monitoring. Export gas is routed into subsea pipelines that tie into the Dutch onshore grid or adjacent hub networks. The platform’s accommodation facilities support periodic crew rotations for maintenance and operations.

platforms.field: The K05 gas fields produce conventional natural gas from shallow marine sandstone reservoirs. The K05 cluster supports multiple installations with central processing at K5P and satellites like K5EN/C, while K5PK augments production by managing pressures and tie-ins.
platforms.intro: A fixed normally unmanned platform installed in 2002 in the K05 cluster, designated as a compressor/pressure-support node. It sits alongside the main K05P hub and aids in maintaining flow pressure and export continuity.
platforms.fac: K5PK’s infrastructure focuses on gas pressure support and network tie-ins rather than primary processing. It includes manifold and boost compression modules to assist field flow assurance and to elevate well outputs toward export conditions. Fluids from local well slots are routed through subsea tie-ins, with core separation and dehydration performed at the primary hub, K5P. K5PK features minimal utility systems typical of unmanned installations, such as power for safety and control systems, chemical dosing units for flow assurance, and remote communication links. The platform enhances field drainage and stabilizes export pressure profiles, ensuring continuous integration with export pipelines feeding the Dutch onshore system.

platforms.field: The K06-C conventional gas field is a shallow-water Dutch North Sea gas accumulation developed with multiple platforms. Reservoirs are Permian Rotliegend sandstones; production infrastructure includes central processing hubs and satellite nodes such as K6C, tied into one another via subsea pipelines.
platforms.intro: A fixed normally unmanned gas wellhead/riser platform in the K06 area of the Dutch North Sea, installed in 1992. Functions as a riser and gathering point for satellite wells, linking into the broader K06 central production infrastructure.
platforms.fac: K6C contains wellheads and riser interfaces for production wells tied back to central processing platforms (e.g., K6P). It does not host significant separation, compression, or dehydration facilities; instead, flows are routed through subsea lines to larger hubs where core processing occurs. Utility systems are limited to unmanned power and control systems for safety, flow control valves, and remote monitoring. K6C acts as a connectivity node within the K06 cluster and supports field drainage across compartments by collecting and transferring hydrocarbons to processing centers. Export from the K06 infrastructure occurs via subsea pipelines linked to regional export networks.

platforms.field: The K06 conventional gas fields comprise shallow water gas reservoirs developed since the early 1990s. These reservoirs produce from Rotliegend sandstones, with central facilities and satellite platforms like K6D enhancing field coverage and drainage.
platforms.intro: A fixed normally unmanned gas wellhead platform in the K06 area, installed in 1991 as part of the K06 field development. It provides production well support and subsea tie-ins feeding the central infrastructure.
platforms.fac: K6D’s facilities include well slots and manifolds connected via subsea flowlines to larger processing hubs such as K6P and possibly K6C. Core processing—separation, dehydration and export compression—occurs on central platforms; K6D’s role is primarily production collection. It is equipped with basic power for instrumentation and safety systems to ensure unmanned operation, as well as flow control and remote monitoring. Produced gas is routed through the K06 network into regional export pipelines. The platform improves drainage and reservoir access across the field.

platforms.field: The K06 conventional gas field system includes multiple installations tied to a central hub; reservoirs are Permian shallow water sands developed with central and satellite platforms to optimize field extraction.
platforms.intro: A fixed normally unmanned satellite wellhead platform within the K06 gas field area, installed in 1992. It serves as a gathering node for selected wells, routing fluids to central processing hubs without major onboard processing.
platforms.fac: K6DN supports production wellheads and subsea connections, with fluids routed through subsea lines to core processing installations (e.g., K6P). It is designed for unmanned remote operation with minimal utility systems—power for control/security systems, emergency shutdowns, and remote communications. Core processing and export compression occur at larger hubs, while K6DN’s infrastructure ensures flow gathering and safe transfer. Export pipelines from the K06 complex integrate into broader Dutch offshore gas trunklines.

platforms.field: The K06 gas field is a conventional natural gas accumulation in the Netherlands sector of the North Sea, developed beginning in 1991. It produces from shallow-water Rotliegend and Zechstein reservoirs typical of Dutch offshore gas geology. The field development includes a central production hub and several satellite platforms including K6GT, K6N and K6P.
platforms.intro: K6GT is a small satellite wellhead platform within the K06 gas field complex on the Dutch Continental Shelf of the North Sea. It functions primarily as a gas production satellite tied into the larger K6 complex infrastructure. The platform is unmanned and connected via subsea flowlines to main production facilities. It was installed as part of K6 development in the 1990s.
platforms.fac: K6GT hosts minimal facilities focused on receiving production from a small number of satellite wells and routing gas via subsea pipelines to the central K6 production complex. There are no full processing modules on K6GT itself; separation, compression, dehydration and export functions are handled at larger nearby platforms (e.g., K6P and K6-C). Utility systems on K6GT are limited to power supplies for control and electrical actuators; detailed power generation and water handling are provided at central facilities. Gas export from the K06 complex typically routes through established export infrastructure to onshore processing via regional pipelines such as the Noordgastransport system. The platform’s design as an unmanned satellite emphasizes compact topsides, minimal habitability modules, and reliance on remote control and monitoring.

platforms.field: The K06 field complex encompasses several conventional gas reservoirs in block K06 of the Dutch continental shelf. These produce from shallow marine sandstone and carbonate sequences typical of Dutch Permian and Triassic stratigraphy. The field includes main production and riser platforms with satellite wellhead platforms like K6N, facilitating reservoir drainage and tie-backs.
platforms.intro: K6N is another small satellite platform in the Dutch North Sea K06 gas field cluster. It serves as a production wellhead and tie-in point feeding into the central K6 complex. Unmanned in operation, it is part of the wider K6 production infrastructure developed in the early 1990s.
platforms.fac: K6N is configured primarily as a wellhead satellite platform, hosting one or more production wells tied back to larger processing facilities in the K6 central complex. It lacks standalone processing; incoming fluids are routed via subsea lines to central processing on the K6P or K6-C towers where separation, compression and dehydration occur. Export from the central complex typically uses regional pipeline networks. Satellite platforms like K6N feature basic power and control systems to operate safety and flow control equipment. There is no accommodation module on K6N as it is designed for unmanned operation.

platforms.field: The K06 gas field is a producing natural gas field in the Netherlands sector of the North Sea. It produces from conventional shallow marine Rotliegend and Zechstein reservoirs and was brought onstream in the early 1990s. The field’s infrastructure includes a central production hub and multiple satellite wellhead platforms.
platforms.intro: K6P is the primary production and processing platform within the K06 gas field development on the Dutch Continental Shelf. Installed as part of the early 1990s development, it receives hydrocarbons from satellite platforms like K6GT and K6N and performs core processing functions. It is integral to compression and export of gas from the K06 complex.
platforms.fac: K6P houses manifold facilities for processing gas from the K06 field, including initial separation, dehydration and gas compression modules. It receives well fluids from its own wells and from satellite platforms (e.g., K6GT, K6N) via subsea flowlines. The platform’s topsides include separation trains, compressors to boost gas for export, and dehydration skids to prepare gas for pipeline transport. Export is typically via the regional Noordgastransport pipeline system to onshore treatment and markets. Power generation systems supply electricity for processing equipment, controls and utilities; water handling is limited to produced water management and minimal utility water distribution. Remote monitoring and control equipment interfaces with shore-based facilities to ensure safe unmanned operation during routine periods.

platforms.field: The K7 field lies in Block K7 of the Southern North Sea, producing conventional natural gas from Rotliegendes sandstone reservoirs. Discovered in 1969 and developed in the late 1970s/early 1980s, it forms part of the K7-K12 cluster of Dutch North Sea gas fields, characterised by high-calorific gas quality and multiple interconnected installations.
platforms.intro: K7-FA-1 is a fixed steel jacket gas production and wellhead platform in the Southern North Sea (Netherlands sector). Installed in the early 1980s, it serves as the primary host for K7 field production and supports gas gathering and export. It connects physically to nearby satellite platforms K7-FD-1 and K7-FB via subsea pipelines.
platforms.fac: K7-FA-1 hosts multiple production wells drilled into the K7 reservoir and serves as a central hub for gathering gas from its own wells and adjacent satellites (K7-FD-1, K7-FB). The topsides include primary separation systems to remove water and condensate, inlet scrubbers, and export compression to maintain pipeline pressure. Gas is exported via an 18-inch pipeline to K8-FA-1 then onward to larger processing hubs. Utilities include on-platform power generation (typically gas turbines or gensets), produced-water handling, and control systems for unmanned or minimally manned operation. Well control is via subsea or platform Christmas trees tied back to the main deck. Structural design is fixed jacket to support drilling, processing modules, and helideck.

platforms.field: The K7 field produces natural gas from Rotliegendes sandstone reservoirs within the Southern North Sea. As part of the K7-K12 group, the field is developed through multiple linked platforms and subsea pipelines. Hydrocarbons are collected at satellites like K7-FB and routed to processing hubs such as K7-FA-1 and onward connections to K8 installations.
platforms.intro: K7-FB is a fixed steel jacket satellite platform located in the K7 block of the Netherlands’ Southern North Sea. Installed in the late 1990s/early 2000s, it functions primarily as a wellhead and gathering platform tied back to the K7-FA-1 central installation for processing. It handles conventional natural gas and associated minor condensate.
platforms.fac: K7-FB comprises wellhead slots for production wells that connect via subsea flowlines to the main K7-FA-1 host. It lacks significant processing and relies on upstream separation and compression at the host. The platform’s topsides are minimal, typically including manifold structures, well control, and metering. Export of unprocessed gas occurs through dedicated pipelines to K7-FA-1. Auxiliary systems include electrical power distribution from the host tie-in, basic utilities for well operations, and remote monitoring/control systems. Its fixed jacket supports well risers and flowlines; water depth in this part of the Southern North Sea is shallow to moderate.

platforms.field: The K7 field’s Rotliegendes sandstone reservoir is part of the broader K7-K12 gas province. Developed with multiple platforms, gas from K7-FD-1 flows towards the central processing installation (K7-FA-1) before export. The field’s gas quality and reservoir characteristics support extended production life through satellite tiebacks.
platforms.intro: K7-FD-1 is a fixed jacket satellite platform in the K7 block of the Dutch Southern North Sea, installed in 1998. It serves as a wellhead and production support node tied back to the main K7-FA-1 platform for processing and export. The facility handles conventional high-calorific natural gas.
platforms.fac: K7-FD-1 is principally a wellhead satellite tied to K7-FA-1 via subsea pipelines. It accommodates several production wells with manifolds routed via flowlines to the host for separation and compression. There is limited topside processing; major facilities remain at K7-FA-1. Structural design is a steel jacket supporting well slots and riser bases. Control systems facilitate remote operation and integration with host processing controls. Power and utilities are minimal, often supplied through the host tie-back. The platform’s function is to extend field drainage and optimize reservoir recovery by accessing wells distant from the main host platform.

platforms.field: The K8 field, in Block K8, produces conventional natural gas from Rotliegendes sandstone, part of the K7-K12 gas province. Discovered circa 1970, the field supports multiple platforms and satellite structures tied to the central K8-FA-1, handling high-calorific gas. Its development reflects early offshore gas exploitation in the Dutch North Sea.
platforms.intro: K8-FA-1 is a major fixed jacket integrated platform in the Netherlands’ Southern North Sea (Block K8), installed in 1977 with production commencing around 1978. It functions as a drilling, production, and processing hub for the K8 field and ties into wider infrastructure, including export pipelines to K14 installations for gas processing.
platforms.fac: K8-FA-1 hosts drilling and production wells, receiving both its own wells and tie-backs from satellites K8-FA-2 and K8-FA-3. The topsides include multiphase separation trains for gas, condensate, and water; gas dehydration and compression modules; and export metering. Post-2000 operations simplified to export dry gas via a major pipeline to the K14-FA-1C processing/compression hub. Export routes to shore integrate into the Dutch gas grid. Utilities encompass onboard power generation (typically gas turbine sets with redundancy), water treatment and injection support, and integrated control systems for unmanned or supervisory control from nearby hubs. Accommodation is typically located on adjacent linked platforms (e.g., K8-FA-1P). Structural design supports drilling derricks, processing modules, and helideck facilities.

platforms.field: The K8 field is centred on a Rotliegendes sandstone gas reservoir developed with K8-FA-1 as the principal hub. Satellites like K8-FA-2 gather production from wells drilled off the main centre and feed into central processing and export routes, forming an integrated field development.
platforms.intro: K8-FA-2 is a fixed jacket satellite platform in the K8 block of the Southern North Sea, installed in the late 1970s. It functions mainly as a drilling and wellhead platform, tied back to the main K8-FA-1 hub for processing and export of conventional natural gas.
platforms.fac: K8-FA-2 accommodates well slots and manifold structures that collect production from its drilled wells. Flowlines tie back to K8-FA-1 where separation, compression, and dehydration occur. The platform’s topside facilities are minimalistic, focusing on well control, metering, and flow assurance equipment. It interfaces with host utilities for power and control communications. The jacket supports well risers and manifold bases; export infrastructure consists of subsea pipelines back to the hub. Remote monitoring and integrated safety systems allow coordinated operations across the K8 cluster.

platforms.field: The K8 field’s geological development is part of the broader K7-K12 gas province. Reservoirs are Rotliegendes sandstones delivering high-calorific gas. Satellites like K8-FA-3 extend reservoir access and tie back to the core K8-FA-1 hub for processing and export.
platforms.intro: K8-FA-3 is a fixed jacket satellite platform in the K8 block of the Southern North Sea, commissioned in the mid-1980s. Serving as a wellhead and gathering node, it ties into the main K8-FA-1 platform for processing and onward export of natural gas produced from the field’s Rotliegendes reservoirs.
platforms.fac: K8-FA-3 includes production well slots and manifolds feeding gas via subsea pipelines to the host. There is no major processing on the platform itself; separation, dehydration, compression, and export metering occur at K8-FA-1. The platform relies on subsea controls, flow assurance measures, and integration into the host’s power and safety systems. Structural elements are fixed jacket legs with riser support. Remote instrumentation and control enable field development efficiency. Export flows join the K8 cluster’s pipeline network to shore or larger processing hubs.

platforms.field: The K9ab field is part of the broader K7–K12 gas province. It produces conventional Rotliegendes gas through satellite platforms tied into central processing and export routes. Reservoir characteristics mirror other K-block developments in shallow offshore Netherlands waters.
platforms.intro: K9ab-B is a fixed offshore gas platform in the Dutch sector of the North Sea, commissioned in 1999. It serves as a satellite production and gathering facility in the K9 area, linking gas production to the K7–K12 field network and onward export infrastructure.
platforms.fac: K9ab-B hosts production wellheads and associated pipeline connections to central processing complexes. Facilities include flow metering, potentially basic separation, and export via subsea pipelines to larger hubs. Electrical power generation supports control systems, safety instrumentation, and essential utilities. Remote operation is typical, with periodic maintenance visits. Subsea infrastructure includes flowlines and risers integrated with corrosion control measures. Control and safety systems include emergency shutdown, fire and gas detection; instrument air and cooling utilities support ongoing operation. Linkages to regional export pipelines enable gas delivery to onshore treatment and distribution networks.

platforms.field: The K9c area sits within the K7–K12 gas field region, exploiting Rotliegendes sandstone reservoirs. Conventional development uses multiple fixed platforms and subsea wells to deliver gas into shared processing systems.
platforms.intro: K9c-A is a fixed offshore gas platform in the Dutch Southern North Sea, installed circa 1987. It acts as a satellite production facility in the K9 area, feeding natural gas into the interconnected K7–K12 field processing and export infrastructure via subsea flowlines.
platforms.rm: incl. compression. Process water being pumped in an empty formation
platforms.fac: K9c-A’s setup comprises wellheads and pipelines routed to central processing installations. The platform is typically unmanned and equipped with flow metering, basic fluid conditioning, and remote control systems. Power is supplied via onboard generation for essential systems, including safety shutdown, communications, and monitoring. Export infrastructure consists of subsea flowlines tied to the regional gas export network. Utility systems cover instrument air, emergency shutdown, and fire/gas detection. Maintenance support is periodic, with vessels servicing structural topsides and subsea components. Integration with neighboring installations permits coordinated field development and export via common pipelines to onshore facilities.

platforms.field: The Katy field lies in Block 44/19b of the UK Southern North Sea producing gas; first gas was achieved in 2013 with field infrastructure tied back to existing systems.
platforms.intro: The Katy platform is a normally unmanned minimal facilities installation in the Katy gas field of the UK Southern North Sea. Installed in 2012, it supports wellheads for production and ties back gas into the Murdoch complex infrastructure, with export onward via the Lincolnshire Offshore Gas Gathering System to Theddlethorpe (historically).
platforms.fac: The Katy platform comprises a three-leg jacket and minimal topsides designed for unmanned operation. It hosts production wellheads and associated Xmas trees, flow control and remote safety systems. Production gas is exported via a ~14-km, 10-inch pipeline tying into the Kelvin subsea tee and then into the Murdoch platform complex. Utility systems include remote safety shutdown, chemical injection for hydrate/corrosion control, and power for local instrumentation. There is no significant hydrocarbon processing on board; fluids flow directly to the Murdoch processing hub for dehydration, compression and conditioning before export to shore. The platform is controlled remotely with periodic maintenance visits, and features basic fire & gas detection, emergency shutdown valves, and subsea control umbilicals linking it to Murdoch.

platforms.field: The Kelvin field is a conventional offshore gas accumulation discovered in 2005 in the Southern North Sea. Gas is sourced from Triassic and Carboniferous sandstone reservoirs, with production beginning in 2007 through a subsea tie-back to the Murdoch complex. It is managed within the CMS gas system, which historically gathered and exported production to the Theddlethorpe terminal onshore.
platforms.intro: Kelvin WHP is a fixed wellhead platform in the Southern UK North Sea, part of the Caister-Murdoch System (CMS) development. Commissioned in 2007, it produces natural gas from the Kelvin gas field in Blocks 44/18b and 44/23b. The platform’s primary role is to host wellheads and initial flowphones, tying back via subsea pipeline to the Murdoch complex for processing and onward export.
platforms.fac: Kelvin WHP’s infrastructure comprises a minimal-facilities wellhead platform with support for one primary production well and associated Christmas tree equipment. Structurally it consists of a three-leg piled steel jacket and topsides designed to support subsea well completions and flow metering facilities. The platform gathers gas at reservoir pressure and routes it into a dedicated subsea pipeline (~12 km) connected to the nearby Murdoch complex, where further aggregation, metering and processing occurred. Kilometric export pipelines from Murdoch historically carried gas to the onshore Theddlethorpe Gas Terminal via the Caister-Murdoch export trunkline. Utility systems on Kelvin WHP are minimal due to its role as a wellhead host; power generation (small diesel or generator sets) supports lighting, control instrumentation, SCADA monitoring and emergency shutdown systems, while safety infrastructure comprises fire and gas detection, emergency blowdown, and basic offshore evacuation provisions. The platform design focused on robust support for remote operations and subsea tie-backs, with corrosion protection, periodic inspection provisions, and interfaces for intervention vessels to access wellheads and manifolds as needed over field life. Decommissioning programmes have been proposed as part of CMS removal, reflecting the system’s mature status while ensuring safe cessation protocols.

platforms.field: The Kilmar field in Block 43/22a produces conventional Carboniferous gas. Discovered in 1992, production began in 2006 with an NUI platform and tie-in pipelines to Trent. As part of the Tyne, Trent and Tors cluster, production volumes declined, leading to export route closure and field shutdown.
platforms.intro: The Kilmar platform is a normally unattended installation (NUI) in the Kilmar gas field of the Southern North Sea, installed in 2005/06. It hosts multiple production wells and exports dry gas via a pipeline to the Trent host platform, with onward export through the Esmond Transmission System to the Bacton Gas Terminal. With export closure at Trent in 2020, Kilmar entered Hydrocarbon Safe status pending decommissioning.
platforms.fac: Kilmar’s installation comprises a fixed steel jacket with topside hosting several production well slots (typically three) with Xmas trees, manifolds, and export flowlines. There is no significant onboard gas processing; dry gas flows via a ~21.3-km, 12-inch export pipeline to the Trent host where compression, dehydration and export to Bacton via the Esmond Transmission System occurred. Utility systems include remotely operated safety shutdown valves, instrument power for control and monitoring, and chemical injection for flow assurance. The platform is unmanned with remote SCADA integration to Trent/shore. Structural design meets UKCS requirements for shallow Southern North Sea conditions, including navigational aids and minimal helideck provisions for maintenance visits. Following market conditions and export closure, Kilmar is in hydrocarbon safe with decommissioning plans progressing.

platforms.field: Kings Quay serves fields in the Green Canyon and Walker Ridge areas of the U.S. Gulf of Mexico. Reservoirs are deepwater turbidite sandstones of Miocene age. These fields are developed via subsea wells tied back to the host facility, representing a hub-style development concept for multiple moderately sized accumulations in ultra-deepwater settings.
platforms.intro: Kings Quay is a deepwater semi-submersible floating production system located in the Gulf of Mexico. It processes oil and gas from multiple subsea tie-backs. First production began in 2022, with the facility acting as a regional hub for several fields. It is designed for high-capacity oil processing and export via shuttle tankers, with gas export through pipeline systems.
platforms.fac: Kings Quay is a semi-submersible FPS designed to process hydrocarbons from multiple subsea fields through an extensive network of flowlines and risers. The facility includes numerous subsea production and injection wells tied back via manifolds. Topsides processing includes multi-stage separation, oil stabilization, gas compression, and dehydration systems. Oil is stored onboard in hull tanks and offloaded to shuttle tankers via offloading systems. Gas is compressed and exported through subsea pipelines to existing Gulf Coast infrastructure. Water handling systems treat produced water for discharge or reinjection. The platform includes high-capacity power generation systems, typically gas turbine-driven, supporting processing and utilities. Advanced control and safety systems manage subsea and topsides operations. The design allows for future tie-backs, making it a regional processing hub. Mooring is achieved via a spread mooring system suited for ultra-deepwater conditions.

platforms.field: Kinneil functions as the processing interface between offshore pipeline delivery and onshore export systems. It handles hydrocarbons collected from many North Sea fields transported through integrated pipelines such as the Forties Pipeline System before forwarding stabilised crude to export terminals or refining networks.
platforms.intro: Kinneil is a land-based oil processing and terminal complex in Grangemouth, Scotland, which receives North Sea crude via pipelines (e.g., Forties Pipeline System). It separates incoming oil into stabilised crude and associated products and serves as a feed hub for onward export to terminals like Hound Point. It is not an offshore platform.
platforms.fac: The Kinneil facility receives crude oil from the FPS pipeline, where it undergoes initial separation to stabilise and treat the fluid to remove gas and lighter ends. The processing comprises multiple separation trains that reduce vapour pressure and strip gas for safe custody transfer. The resulting stabilised crude is segregated for export via pipeline to Dalmeny and Hound Point or onward to refining/chemical complexes. Gas streams may be routed into local distribution networks or flared where necessary. Utilities include steam/electric power systems for heaters and pumps, water handling, flare and safety systems, control rooms with process automation, and storage buffer tanks. Metrology and custody transfer systems ensure accuracy for commercial transactions. The design emphasises reliable throughput capacity and pressure/flow control to maintain specification consistency for export and downstream use.

platforms.field: The Kittiwake oil field lies in Block-21/18 at about 85–90-m water depth. The field produces Upper Jurassic Fulmar Formation oil and associated gas. With the field’s own production declining, the platform now processes fluids from satellite Goosander, Grouse, Gadwall, Mallard and related areas, collectively known as the Greater Kittiwake Area.
platforms.intro: Kittiwake A is a fixed steel production and processing platform in Block-21/18 of the UK Central North Sea, commissioned in 1990. It initially produced hydrocarbons from the Kittiwake field and now serves as a hub for the Greater Kittiwake Area, receiving tie-backs from satellite fields. Drilling facilities were decommissioned in 2009.
platforms.fac: Kittiwake A’s steel jacket supports production and processing facilities configured for multiphase separation, gas compression and water handling. While original drilling facilities have been removed, the platform continues to receive hydrocarbons from subsea tie-backs. Fluids are processed through stabilisation and separation trains; oil is metered and exported via the Greater Kittiwake Area export pipeline to the Forties Pipeline System through the Unity platform, and processed gas is utilised for fuel/gas lift with surplus exported via a small diameter line to the SEGAL gas pipeline. Produced water treatment facilities handle effluent per regulatory standards. Utilities include onboard power generation, HVAC, firewater and safety systems, and control rooms coordinating operations and export interfaces. Accommodation supports personnel, and control and safety systems ensure stable long-term operation of multiple field tie-backs into the hub facility.

platforms.field: The Kollsnes facility sits near Bergen and receives rich gas through Gassco-operated pipelines from Troll and other Norwegian continental shelf fields. It extracts NGL (ethane, propane, butane, naphtha) for hydrocarbon liquids markets and compresses dry gas for export via Statpipe, Europipe and Zeepipe.
platforms.intro: Kollsnes is a major onshore gas processing plant in western Norway, operational since 1996, processing rich gas from Troll, Kvitebjørn and Visund fields. It separates natural gas liquids (NGL) from dry gas, compresses processed gas and sends it into continental export pipelines. It interfaces with offshore export pipelines and the Vestprosess NGL export system to Mongstad.
platforms.fac: Kollsnes comprises multiple process trains for gas dehydration, mercury removal, NGL extraction, fractionation interfaces, and high-pressure gas compression. Rich inlet gas arrives via trunk pipelines; NGL components are separated and sent into the Vestprosess pipeline to Mongstad for further fractionation, storage, or export. Dry gas is compressed and conditioned for export into the integrated Gassled pipeline network (Statpipe, Europipe, Zeepipe). Utilities include power generation, heat recovery, flare systems, water treatment, and control rooms coordinating fieldwide pipeline operations. Safety systems cover emergency shutdowns, gas detection, and compressor protection. As a stable midstream hub, Kollsnes supports long-term processing capacity linked directly with offshore infrastructure and European gas markets.

platforms.field: The Kollsnes site is part of the Troll–Kvitebjørn–Visund gas processing chain in the North Sea and Norwegian Sea region. It handles gas landed from Troll and other fields, removes condensate and NGLs, and prepares dry gas for export. Kollsnes supports export networks into Europe, linking to major pipeline systems that carry Norwegian gas to continental destinations.
platforms.intro: Kollsnes refers to the industrial park and associated gas processing and export infrastructure at Kollsnes on the west coast of Norway. It is an onshore natural gas processing facility handling dry gas and natural gas liquids (NGL). Commissioned in 1996, it plays a central midstream role in handling gas from multiple offshore fields before export to European markets.
platforms.fac: Kollsnes comprises large gas separation, dehydration, and NGL extraction trains fed by pipelines from offshore fields such as Troll, Kvitebjørn, and Visund. Gas arriving at Kollsnes is processed to remove liquids and water, compressed to export specifications, and then routed into export pipelines such as Statpipe, Zeepipe, Europipe, and Franpipe. The plant also includes significant utility systems — high-pressure gas compressors, dehydration units, NGL fractionation support equipment, power generation and distribution systems, flare and safety control infrastructure, and metering for export contracts. Kollsnes integrates with Vestprosess (liquid export infrastructure) and supplies dry gas to domestic and European markets. The site’s design emphasizes continuous operation, redundancy in compression and separation trains, and robust control and safety systems typical of major onshore processing hubs.

platforms.field: The Kraka field lies adjacent to the Dan oil field in the Danish sector. Discovered in the late 20th century, it produces from chalk reservoirs with both oil and gas components. It was developed with a small platform and horizontal wells, tying back to Dan for processing.
platforms.intro: Kraka is an unmanned satellite wellhead platform serving the Kraka field, a small oil and gas accumulation in the Danish North Sea developed as a satellite of the Dan field. The installation supports oil and associated gas production and exports to central Dan facilities for processing.
platforms.fac: Kraka’s infrastructure comprises a fixed unmanned wellhead platform with production wells drilled into the chalk reservoir. The installation lacks major processing trains, exporting unprocessed oil and gas via subsea pipeline to the Dan FA platform. Well control and basic electrical power are provided topside for monitoring and control, with remote automation linked to Dan’s control center. Pipelines and umbilicals extend between Kraka and Dan for production fluid export and control signal transmission. Utility systems are minimal, limited to emergency power, instrumentation, and safety monitoring systems. This configuration reflects the satellite role of Kraka in a more extensive hub network anchored by Dan’s processing capabilities.

platforms.field: The Kraken oil field lies in the East Shetland Basin and produces heavy oil from Upper Jurassic sandstone reservoirs. Discovered in 1985, the field is characterized by viscous crude and relatively shallow reservoirs. Development uses subsea wells tied back to a central FPSO with shuttle tanker export.
platforms.intro: The Kraken FPSO is a floating production, storage and offloading vessel located in the UK Central North Sea, Block 9/2a. Installed and commissioned in 2017, it provides full processing, storage, and offloading for the Kraken heavy oil field. The FPSO is permanently moored and receives production from a network of subsea wells via flexible risers.
platforms.fac: The Kraken FPSO supports subsea production and injection wells via risers and umbilicals. Processing facilities include three-phase separation, crude oil heating, stabilization, and produced water treatment. Due to the heavy oil properties, extensive heating and flow assurance systems are installed throughout the processing train. Produced water is treated and reinjected for pressure support. Associated gas is used for fuel, with surplus managed through controlled systems. The FPSO provides large crude storage capacity and offloads stabilized oil to shuttle tankers in tandem configuration. Utilities include power generation, seawater lift, firewater and deluge systems, inert gas systems, chemical injection, and integrated control and safety systems. The vessel is turret-moored, allowing it to weathervane, and is designed for long-term operation in North Sea conditions.

platforms.field: The Kristin field, discovered in 1997, lies in ~370-m water depth southwest of the Åsgard  area. Reservoirs are Jurassic sandstones with high pressure and temperature. It was developed with subsea templates tied back to the central platform. Production includes gas and condensate exported via pipeline systems to onshore facilities.
platforms.intro: The Kristin installation is a semi-submersible production platform in the Haltenbanken area of the Norwegian Sea, producing gas and condensate since 2005. It serves as a processing hub and host for subsea tie-backs such as Tyrihans and Maria, with export connectivity to shore.
platforms.fac: Kristin’s semi-submersible platform processes hydrocarbons from multiple subsea wells drilled on four 4-slot templates. Primary separation of gas and liquids occurs topside; condensate is stabilised and routed to storage or to the Åsgard  C storage vessel for shipment. Rich gas is exported via the Åsgard  Transport System (ÅTS) to the Kårstø processing terminal onshore Norway, where further conditioning and liquids extraction occur. The platform utilities include gas compression to meet export pipeline pressure requirements, produced water handling, power generation, heat recovery, and safety and control systems. Subsea infrastructure includes flowlines and umbilicals connecting templates and satellite fields. Kristin also supports ongoing development tie-backs under the Kristin South project, extending field life and throughput.

platforms.field: The Kvitebjørn field, discovered in 1994, lies in the North Sea and produces gas and condensate from deep reservoirs. The development includes integrated platform processing for export via pipelines to onshore gas terminals at Kollsnes (gas) and Mongstad (condensate).
platforms.intro: Kvitebjørn is a fixed steel jacket platform in the northern North Sea producing gas and condensate since 2004. It processes hydrocarbons from its own wells and serves as a processing point for gas from fields such as Valemon, exporting to onshore facilities for further transport.
platforms.fac: Kvitebjørn’s jacket platform hosts processing trains for gas and condensate separation, compression to pipeline pressure, dehydration and metering systems. Gas exports via sub-sea pipeline to Kollsnes feed into the national grid; condensate travels via pipeline to Mongstad for further fractionation. Wellstreams from Kvitebjørn’s wells enter multiphase separators topside before phase separation; water handling systems manage produced water. Utilities include power generation, safety and fire systems, and control systems integrated with the Gassco transport network. The installation accommodates accommodation modules, helideck facilities, and redundancy in power and control systems to support long-term operation in ~190-m water depth.

platforms.field: Kårstø handles hydrocarbons from ~30 offshore fields including Statfjord, Åsgard  and Sleipner. Its processing trains strip liquids and condense components for storage, with dry gas fed into pipeline networks like Statpipe and Europipe II. Propane and other liquids are exported globally by ship.
platforms.intro: Kårstø is a large onshore natural gas and condensate processing complex near Susort in Rogaland, Norway. Operational since 1985, it receives rich gas and condensate from northern North Sea fields via Statpipe and Åsgard  Transport, separates and fractionates into methane, ethane, propane, butanes, naphtha and stabilised condensate, and exports products to European markets and by ship.
platforms.fac: The Kårstø complex comprises multiple separation and fractionation trains for rich gas and condensate arriving from offshore pipelines. Facilities separate methane (dry gas), ethane, propane, isobutane, normal butane, naphtha and stabilised condensate. Propane is stored in large underground caverns; other liquids are held in tanks for ship export. Dry gas is exported via major pipelines including Statpipe and Europipe II to Germany and beyond. Utilities include power generation (primarily fuel gas), compressors, heat recovery, water and effluent systems, and comprehensive control rooms. The plant’s control systems manage 24/7 operations, emissions monitoring and safety shutdowns. Kårstø also hosts fractionation units for ethane and condensate, and interfaces with midstream networks for broad European distribution.

platforms.field: The L10 gas field is a large conventional natural gas accumulation in the Southern North Sea, discovered in 1970 and producing since 1976. Rotliegendes sandstone reservoirs deliver high-calorific gas; the field acts as a hub for multiple satellite platforms.
platforms.intro: L10-AC is a fixed offshore gas compression platform in the L10 gas field on the Dutch continental shelf, installed in 1987. As part of the L10-A platform complex, it supports natural gas compression for export and intra-field boosting. It is bridge-linked into the core L10 hub.
platforms.fac: L10-AC’s facilities are dedicated to gas compression, receiving conditioned gas from wellhead and riser platforms within the L10-A complex. It increases pressure to meet export pipeline requirements and balance flow to the main L10 processing trains. The platform ties into pipe networks and bridges that link to L10-AP and L10-AD, supporting integrated field operations. It houses compression trains, control systems, and utility modules (power generation, cooling, safety shutdown systems). Gas is exported from the hub via the 36-inch Noordgastransport trunk line to onshore facilities in Uithuizen after conditioning and compression. Its unmanned design uses remote monitoring and periodic service calls.

platforms.field: Within the L10 gas field, L10-AD accesses Rotliegendes sandstone gas reservoirs. This field has been a major Dutch offshore gas contributor since 1976 and acts as a production and processing hub for the area.
platforms.intro: L10-AD is the original drilling and wellhead platform of the L10-A complex on the Dutch North Sea shelf, installed in 1974. It hosts production wells and bridge connections to adjacent L10-A modules including L10-AP and L10-AR.
platforms.rm: incl. compression. Two skimmer tanks present, that are used seperately and can be cleaned.
platforms.fac: L10-AD includes drilled production wells feeding gas into manifold systems. It interfaces with the L10-A complex’s processing and riser modules via steel bridges, facilitating centralized separation and export. On-platform systems include wellhead control, flow metering, and safety shutdown (ESD) networks. While it does not host large processing trains, AD is integral to the riser and header configuration feeding into central dehydration, compression, and dehydration facilities located on adjacent platforms. Utilities power instrumentation, communications and safety systems. Export gas flows through the L10 hub into the Noordgastransport pipeline to shore, and integration with satellite ties enables optimized field production.

platforms.field: The L10 field’s Rotliegendes sandstone gas reservoirs are accessed from AP via wellheads and satellite tie-ins; production began in 1976 and has continued into the present as part of a multi-platform system.
platforms.intro: L10-AP is the main production platform within the L10-A complex, installed in 1975. It serves as the primary gas production and processing platform in the field hub, linked by bridges to L10-AD (wellheads), L10-AC (compression), and L10-AR (riser).
platforms.fac: L10-AP’s facilities encompass gas gathering from AD and satellite platforms, primary separation, dehydration, metering, and conditioning for export. It is the central processing node in the L10-A complex, with integrated compression from AC and riser support from AR. AP’s topsides include separation vessels, dehydration skids, metering trains, and control systems managed via DCS, with ESD for safety integrity. Utility modules supply power generation, firewater, and water handling. Conditioned gas is fed into the 36-inch Noordgastransport pipeline to Uithuizen onshore. The platform’s design supports long-term, stable processing and export operations with periodic maintenance access.

platforms.field: The L10 field’s gas reservoirs in Rotliegendes sandstones are the production target. The field is a long-lived Dutch offshore gas producer, developed with multiple platforms and subsea ties.
platforms.intro: L10-AR is the riser and reception platform of the L10-A complex, installed in 1975. It provides riser connections for subsea flowlines and bridges into the main L10 processing hub.
platforms.fac: L10-AR’s role centers on handling incoming riser lines from subsea completions and cross-field pipelines. It collects high-pressure gas flows and feeds them into the L10-A main processing facility at AP. On-platform infrastructure includes riser manifolds, emergency shutdown systems, and flow control valves. While minimal processing is undertaken locally, AR supports integrated flow management into central dehydration and compression trains located at AP and AC. Utilities provide instrumentation power, safety systems, and structural support for risers and bridges. Export pathways from L10-AR ultimately connect into the central L10 hub followed by the Noordgastransport trunk to shore.

platforms.field: The L10 field produces conventional Rotliegendes gas. Satellite platforms like L10-B enable wide area production with centralized treatment and export via the L10-A hub.
platforms.intro: L10-B is a fixed offshore wellhead and production platform in the L10 gas field, installed in 1974. It serves as a satellite to the L10-A complex, delivering gas via pipeline to the core hub.
platforms.fac: L10-B’s facilities comprise multiple production wells with flowlines and manifold connections. Produced gas is routed via subsea pipelines to the L10-A central processing complex for separation, dehydration, and export. On-platform systems provide well control, basic metering, and emergency shutdown. Minimal processing occurs locally; conditioning and export compression are centralized at AP and AC. Utilities include instrumentation power, control systems, and safety features. Gas from L10-B is integrated into the field network and exported to shore via the Noordgastransport pipeline.

platforms.field: As part of the L10 field, BB accesses Rotliegendes sandstone reservoirs; its development augments production capacity by feeding wells into the satellite-to-hub network centered on L10-A.
platforms.intro: L10-BB is a fixed wellhead satellite platform in the L10 gas field, installed in 1980. It supports additional well slots tied into the L10-B satellite gathering system, feeding into the L10-A hub.
platforms.fac: L10-BB has production wellheads and manifold infrastructure linked to L10-B and onward pipelines into the L10-A complex. It provides flow control, basic metering and emergency shutdown capability. There is no major processing on the platform; it functions as a gathering node dispatching gas to central dehydration and compression facilities at AP and AC. Utilities include local instrumentation power and safety systems. The export path remains through the L10 hub into the North Sea trunk pipeline network to Uithuizen.

platforms.field: L10-E taps the same Rotliegendes reservoirs that feed the broader L10 field. This field’s multi-platform architecture supports extensive production and export capacity.
platforms.intro: L10-E is a fixed offshore satellite gas production platform in the L10 gas field, installed in 1977. It delivers gas via pipeline to the L10-A central processing hub (AP/AC/AR) for conditioning and export.
platforms.fac: L10-E’s infrastructure includes well slots with associated manifolds and flowlines that tie into subsea pipeline connections leading to the L10-A hub. Local facilities include production control, metering, and emergency shutdown systems; there is no significant on-platform gas treatment. All separation, dehydration, and export compression occur at the main processing installations (AP/AC). Utility systems support instrumentation and remote monitoring. Export gas enters the Noordgastransport pipeline network to onshore receiving facilities after conditioning in the central hub.

platforms.field: The L10 gas field is a large conventional natural gas field in the Southern North Sea, discovered in 1970 and producing since 1976. Reservoirs are Upper Rotliegendes sandstones on the Dutch continental shelf, developed with multiple wellhead and hub platforms.
platforms.intro: L10-EE is a fixed natural gas production platform in the L10 gas field on the Dutch continental shelf, originally installed in the 1980s as part of development of the L10 area — a major shallow gas hub. It supports production wellheads and tie-ins into central processing and export infrastructure linked to the L10-A Complex.
platforms.fac: L10-EE functions primarily as a satellite wellhead and collection point within the larger L10 gas field. It comprises a steel jacket with well slots tied into subsea and platform gatherers that feed gas to L10-A Complex and nearby compression/processing installations. On-platform equipment includes wellheads, flow control and metering systems, basic pressure and choke control, and emergency shutdown (ESD) systems. There is minimal gas processing on the structure itself, with conditioning and dehydration handled at the central L10-A and associated processing facilities before export via the Noordgastransport pipeline system to onshore gas treatment plants. Utilities are limited to instrument power and remote monitoring systems; periodic maintenance is conducted via supply vessels and helicopters.

platforms.field: The L10 field is a substantial conventional gas accumulation in the Southern North Sea. The reservoir comprises Rotliegendes sandstones producing high-calorific gas tied into Dutch offshore infrastructure.
platforms.intro: L10-F is a fixed wellhead gas platform within the L10 gas field, installed in 1980 to support production from nearby reservoir wells. It is connected by pipeline to the L10-A hub platform for further processing and export of gas via the Noordgastransport system.
platforms.fac: The L10-F platform includes a steel jacket supporting multiple well slots for gas wells. Produced gas is routed from wellheads through manifolds and pipeline tie-backs to the L10-A Complex for separation, dehydration and compression. On-platform facilities are limited to production control, metering and safety systems (ESD, remote monitoring). The installation has no major processing or compression trains; such functions are centralized at the field hub (L10-A), where topside separation and export compression prepare gas for export. Power for instrumentation and communications is provided locally, and utilities include basic firewater and monitoring systems. Export infrastructure ties into the North Sea trunk lines to shore.

platforms.field: The installation produces gas from the L10 field’s Rotliegendes sandstone reservoirs. This field is a major Dutch offshore gas producer with long-term development via multiple platforms and subsea wells.
platforms.intro: L10-L is a fixed natural gas production platform in the Dutch L10 block, commissioned in 1988 to support gas recovery and feed the L10 central processing complex. It serves as a satellite wellhead installation integrated into the L10 network.
platforms.fac: L10-L’s facilities consist of multiple wells tied into manifolds and pipelines feeding into the main L10 hub infrastructure. The platform itself provides well access, flow control and basic metering; conditioning (separation, dehydration) and export compression are carried out at central processing installations such as L10-A. On-platform utilities support instrumentation, emergency shutdown systems, and periodic service access; there are no large on-platform processing trains. Gas exported from the L10 area enters the Noordgastransport pipeline system to onshore treatment facilities.

platforms.field: The L10-M field sits within the broader L10 gas accumulation, producing conventional gas from Rotliegendes reservoirs in shallow Southern North Sea waters. The L10 gas field is a long-lived, multi-platform development.
platforms.intro: L10-M is a fixed platform in the Dutch L10 gas field, installed in 2000 as part of the mature L10 development. It functions as a satellite gas production installation feeding the central L10 process hub and export infrastructure.
platforms.fac: L10-M hosts a set of gas wells with associated flowlines and manifolds. Produced gas is sent via subsea/pipeline tie-ins to a central processing installation (L10-A) for separation, dehydration, and compression prior to export. On-platform systems include wellhead and flow control, metering, and safety shutdown. Limited utilities support instrumentation and remote operation; no significant gas treatment or compression modules are present locally. Gas is routed into the Noordgastransport pipeline for onshore delivery after conditioning at the hub.

platforms.field: The L11b-A field lies in the southern Dutch North Sea and produces conventional natural gas (with condensate) from shallow reservoirs. Production began in the 1980s and continues as part of broader L11 and adjacent L8-D developments, feeding regional export infrastructure.
platforms.intro: L11-B refers to the L11b-A oil and gas production platform in the Dutch North Sea, commissioned in the mid-1980s to produce hydrocarbons from the L11b-A field. It serves as a central processing hub for nearby developments in the L11b and L8-D area, with export connections to trunk pipelines.
platforms.fac: L11b-A’s facilities include multiple production wells drilled from the jacket, feeding into central topside separation and processing modules. The platform handles primary gas separation, condensate stabilization, and metering before export via subsea pipelines into wider Dutch gas trunk systems. It also supports drilling activities and serves as a host for subsea tie-backs and remote platforms. Utilities comprise power generation, water and fire systems, accommodation, and integrated control/safety systems. Export gas is routed to Den Helder and integrated into national networks via the Noordgastransport and NOGAT pipeline systems. The platform has been modified over time to support production consistency and field tie-ins, reflecting stable mid-life operations in the Dutch sector.

platforms.field: The L13 field is a conventional shallow-water gas accumulation in Block L13 offshore the Netherlands, developed with several fixed platforms feeding gas from Rotliegendes reservoirs. The field comprises L13-FC-1, L13-FD-1, L13-FE-1, with production tied into Dutch export networks.
platforms.intro: L13-FC-1 is a fixed normally unmanned gas production/wellhead platform in Block L13 of the Dutch North Sea, installed in 1986. It produces natural gas and serves as a gathering point for satellite wells in the L13 cluster, exporting via subsea pipelines to regional export infrastructure such as K15-FA-1. It connects physically to nearby L13 installations.
platforms.fac: L13-FC-1 hosts multiple production well slots connected to reservoir zones via wellheads and flowlines. Topside facilities include flow metering and basic phase separation before export. Gas is conditioned to meet pipeline specifications and routed through subsea export lines to larger hubs (e.g., K15-FA-1). Electrical generation provides power for remote monitoring, control (SCADA), and safety systems including emergency shutdown and fire/gas detection. Utilities include instrument air and essential support services for normally unmanned operations. Subsea infrastructure comprises risers, flowlines, and corrosion protection systems. Periodic vessel-based maintenance supports structural integrity and pipeline inspection. Integration with adjacent platforms facilitates coordinated field development and stable export to the Dutch gas grid.

platforms.field: Operated within the L13 conventional gas field complex, L13-FD-1 accesses Rotliegendes sandstone gas. The field uses multiple fixed platforms to drain reservoir compartments, with gas routed into export pipelines to onshore processing facilities.
platforms.intro: L13-FD-1 is a fixed, primarily manned satellite gas platform in the L13 block of the Dutch North Sea, installed in 1988. It gathers natural gas from assigned wells and routes production into L13-FC-1 and onward export networks. It is one of the satellite installations supporting the wider L13 field network.
platforms.fac: L13-FD-1’s infrastructure includes production wellheads, manifolds, and flowlines tied into the L13-FC-1 gathering system. Minimal topside separation may be present, with gas routed to central hubs for full processing. Electrical power supports control and safety systems including emergency shutdown and fire/gas detection. Utilities include instrument air and essential monitoring. Subsea pipelines connect to export routes feeding the Dutch onshore grid. Periodic maintenance by service vessels sustains topside and subsea assets. Integration into the L13 cluster allows efficient reservoir management and export via established pipeline infrastructure.

platforms.field: The field served by L13-FE-1 is a conventional offshore gas accumulation in Block L13, developed via multiple fixed installations draining Rotliegendes sandstone reservoirs. Gas is collected and exported to onshore facilities.
platforms.intro: L13-FE-1 is a fixed, manned gas satellite platform in the L13 block of the Dutch North Sea, commissioned in 1989. It produces natural gas from assigned wells and feeds into the L13-FC-1 and wider export infrastructure. It is part of the L13 field’s network of satellites.
platforms.fac: L13-FE-1’s facilities include wellheads and flowlines tying into L13-FC-1’s gathering system. Basic topside equipment supports metering and routing of gas to central compression and processing hubs. Power generation and control systems enable remote monitoring, emergency shutdown and safety functions. Utilities include instrument air and essential services. Subsea flowlines connect to the export pipeline network sending gas to onshore treatment and distribution systems. Periodic maintenance sustains platform and subsea integrity. Integration with neighboring L13 platforms ensures coordinated field development.

platforms.field: The L13-FI field lies in Block L13 offshore the Netherlands in shallow water, producing conventional gas from Rotliegendes reservoirs as part of the broader L13 gas development.
platforms.intro: L13-FI-1 is a fixed unmanned monotower gas platform in Block L13 of the Dutch North Sea, commissioned in 2017. It produces natural gas and supports chemical injection facilities. Produced gas is exported via a 12- pipeline to the K15-FA-1 complex. Communication and control are linked to nearby platforms.
platforms.fac: L13-FI-1’s infrastructure is based on a monotower design with a single deck and monopile foundation. It includes production wells and chemical injection skids to support flow assurance. Produced gas is routed through a 12- export pipeline to the K15-FA-1 processing hub. A piggyback line facilitates import of production chemicals. Electrical power generation and remote control systems support SCADA, safety shutdown and communications. Utilities include instruments and monitoring systems tailored for unmanned operation. The design emphasizes compactness and ease of installation, interfacing with existing IntraField infrastructure to export gas efficiently. Periodic service vessel visits ensure topside and subsea asset integrity and maintenance.

platforms.field: The L15 gas field produces conventional natural gas from reservoirs northwest of Den Helder. It was developed in the late 20th century alongside nearby small field infrastructure tying into national export pipelines.
platforms.intro: L15-FA-1 is a fixed offshore gas production platform in the Dutch North Sea, historically producing gas from the L15 field since the early 1990s. It is integrated into regional processing and export infrastructure feeding the NOGAT pipeline system.
platforms.fac: L15-FA-1 is equipped with production wells, gas separation, and initial conditioning facilities, enabling export of treated gas via subsea pipelines. The platform’s topsides historically handled separation and dehydration ahead of export to onshore facilities via the NOGAT system, which connects multiple Dutch offshore gas developments to the gas treatment plant at Den Helder. Utilities include platform power generation, water and fire systems, safety shutdowns, and integrated controls for sustained operations. As part of a mature field, it interfaces with adjacent satellite wells and subsea completions, receiving and delivering production flows into the export network.

platforms.field: The L2-FA gas field was discovered in 1968 and commenced production via L2-FA-1 in 1992. It produces conventional gas from Rotliegendes reservoirs offshore the Netherlands, with L2-FB later tied back into the platform.
platforms.intro: L2-FA-1 is a fixed offshore gas production platform in block L2 of the Dutch North Sea, brought onstream in 1992. It produces natural gas and serves as the central processing and export node for the L2-FA and associated L2-FB fields. The platform has accommodation and helicopter facilities.
platforms.fac: L2-FA-1 hosts multiple production wells with wellheads tied to integrated topside processing modules that separate gas from liquids and water. Facilities include dehydration and metering to meet export standards. The platform supports accommodation, helicopter operations, electrical generation, and control systems for ongoing production. Utilities cover instrument air, cooling, and safety systems such as emergency shutdown and fire/gas detection. Export infrastructure includes subsea pipelines connecting to the NGT/Nogat trunklines to onshore gas treatment and distribution systems. The installation’s design supports long-term operations, with robust structural and subsea integrity measures and periodic maintenance performed by offshore support vessels.

platforms.field: The L4 segment of the L4-L7 gas fields is an established natural gas accumulation in the Netherlands sector of the North Sea, discovered in the 1970s and developed with multiple platforms. Reservoir rocks are Upper Rotliegend sandstones typical of the area. L4A has been a core producing platform for L4 developments since the early 1980s.
platforms.intro: L4A is a fixed production platform in the L4 portion of the L4-L7 gas field complex on the Dutch Continental Shelf. Installed in the early 1980s, it functions as a production and export hub for gas from multiple subsea and adjacent platforms. It is normally unmanned and tied into nearby hubs such as the K6 complex.
platforms.fac: L4A receives gas from its own production wells and subsea completions (e.g. L4G) and routes fluids to processing at central facilities in the area. It serves as a collection and export point; final gas conditioning (drying, compression) is typically done at central complexes such as K6-CC2 or L7/L10 hubs. The platform is equipped with wellheads, risers, basic manifolding and flow control valves. Utility systems on L4A include power for instrumentation and safety systems, with main power and processing handling at larger hubs. Export pipelines link L4A to regional trunklines and offshore treatment centers, feeding gas into onshore grids. Because L4A operates unmanned, remote control and monitoring systems are critical for safe operations.

platforms.field: The L4-L7 gas fields form a contiguous gas-bearing system in the Dutch North Sea, developed since the 1970s with multiple platforms. Production is primarily from Rotliegend sandstones. L4PN supplements production from the L4 portion of the field, enhancing reservoir drainage.
platforms.intro: L4PN is a satellite production platform within the L4-L7 gas field complex on the Dutch Continental Shelf. Installed in the late 1990s, it collects hydrocarbons from a subset of wells and ties back to main platforms like L4A. It is typically unmanned.
platforms.fac: L4PN functions as a collection platform feeding gas to larger processing and export hubs. It hosts satellite wellheads and associated manifold systems; it does not include full separation or compression facilities. Fluids are routed via subsea or bridge-linked pipelines to main platforms such as L4A or onward to regional processing centers. L4PN supports basic power and control infrastructure for safe unmanned operation, with main utilities provided at central platforms. Gas export flows through integrated pipeline networks to shore via regional hubs.

platforms.field: The L5 block includes conventional natural gas reservoirs in Lower Permian Rotliegendes sandstone beneath the Southern North Sea. The L5-B field was discovered in 1999 and developed with satellite platforms producing natural gas. Nearby fields like L5-C and export hubs support regional development.
platforms.intro: A normally unmanned fixed satellite gas production platform in block L5 of the Dutch Southern North Sea, installed to develop the L5 block gas reservoirs. Production started in the early 2000s (circa 2003). L5-B handled processing and export tie-in duties, often connected to adjacent infrastructure such as L8-P4 for onward export. It is subject to decommissioning planning.
platforms.fac: L5-B’s infrastructure comprised well slots for production wells tied to a topside with minimal processing (separation, gas conditioning). Produced gas was piped via short subsea lines to platform L8-P4 or similar host infrastructure for further processing/export. The platform’s utility systems supported unmanned operation with remote control, limited gas dehydration, and chemical injection for flow assurance. Power was likely via onboard generators sized to support minimal control and transfer systems. Its design reflected a satellite link role in a cluster development for multiple small gas accumulations.

platforms.field: The L05-C gas field is a conventional offshore gas accumulation in the Netherlands discovered in 2003 and brought into production by 2006. The reservoir is Rotliegendes sandstone, typical of Southern North Sea gas fields, and has proven extractable gas reserves in the low billions of cubic meters.
platforms.intro: A fixed satellite gas platform developed to produce gas from the L05-C gas field in the Dutch Southern North Sea, placed into service in the mid-2000s. L5-C exported hydrocarbons through subsea pipelines to nearby host facilities (e.g., L8-P4) and supported gas conditioning for export.
platforms.fac: L5-C hosted production wells tied into topside separation/conditioning equipment and subsea export infrastructure via pipeline to a larger processing hub such as L8-P4. Facilities included basic gas separation and metering for export, chemical injection for hydrate control, and remote operation utilities. Power was provided by small diesel generators supporting unmanned control systems. The installation functioned as a satellite node in a broader cluster development, with export via subsea pipelines feeding into regional high-pressure networks.

platforms.field: The L5-FA field produces conventional natural gas from reservoirs offshore northwest of Den Helder. It was developed alongside other small fields and integrated into the national pipeline network (NOGAT) for export to onshore treatment plants.
platforms.intro: L5-FA-1 is a fixed gas production platform in the Dutch North Sea, operational since the early 1990s and producing gas from the L5-FA field. It connects to subsea pipelines feeding processing and export infrastructure to shore.
platforms.fac: Facilities on L5-FA-1 include production wellheads with associated manifold and flow control, initial gas separation, dehydration and metering ahead of export to central processing and export infrastructure. The platform supports utilities such as power generation, firewater, safety shutdown (ESD), and control systems for remote operation. Gas exported from the platform enters subsea trunk pipelines that deliver to onshore facilities for further treatment and delivery to the Dutch gas grid.

platforms.field: The L5a-D field is a deep, high-pressure gas accumulation in the Dutch sector. Production includes gas (via L5a-D4 and other wells) with flows transported through offshore infrastructure into national export routes.
platforms.intro: L5a-D is a fixed offshore gas production platform in the Dutch North Sea, installed around 2013 to develop the L5a-D field. It has been connected to high-pressure, high-temperature wells and exports gas via pipeline networks tied into the NOGAT export system.
platforms.fac: L5a-D comprises an unmanned platform with gas production wellheads, flowlines and basic processing modules. It handles initial separation and export preparation before injecting gas into pipelines leading to central processing or directly into export trunk lines (NOGAT). On-platform utilities include control systems, emergency shutdown (ESD), remote monitoring, and minimal instrument power. The platform’s infrastructure supports periodic servicing and integration with the broader Dutch offshore gas network enabling sustained export.

platforms.field: The L6-B field is a small natural gas prospect in ~30–35-m water depth on the Netherlands Continental Shelf. Gas is produced from shallow Permian or Slochteren Formation sandstones typical of the Southern North Sea and exported via subsea pipeline to L8-P4 for processing and onward transport.
platforms.intro: L6-B is a small unmanned “minimum facility” gas production platform in the Dutch sector of the Southern North Sea, installed in 2014 and producing since 2015. It supports primary natural gas extraction with very limited local processing, tied directly to the larger L8-P4 platform via pipeline and umbilical for control and power.
platforms.fac: L6-B’s structure comprises a minimalist steel wellhead and production platform anchored by suction piles with a light topside capable of accommodating two wells. There is no accommodation or helideck. Because processing on L6-B is minimal, produced gas flows immediately via a subsea pipeline (~8-inch) to L8-P4 where separation and compression occur. An electrical and control umbilical (~19.5-km) from L8-P4 supplies power, controls, and monitoring to the remote L6-B. Utilities on L6-B are limited to essential subsea control umbilical interfaces, wellhead control, and flow metering; higher-order processing and export conditioning are delegated to the host platform L8-P4.
